text: The year was 1889, and the last natural forest on Earth was a spectacle that many traveled miles to behold. Eli, a young botanist, stood in awe among the ancient trees, a leather-bound journal in hand as he recorded notes about species that had become legends. This sacred grove, unbeknownst to him, was about to become the centerpiece of a historic preservation effort that would challenge the industrial metropolis encroaching upon the natural world. The city, dominated by the iron lattice of the Eiffel Tower in France, loomed nearby, its smokestacks choking the sky, while Eli clung to the hope that nature’s last breath might be saved from the relentless march of progress.
